column1: # Tutorial Chapter 5, Lesson 16: a macro that prints data.
# Author a macro that performs the slash-command sequence
# `/Print File <path> Range A1..B1 Go Quit`. Bind it to a
# Alt-letter doesn't apply), then invoke it via Alt-F3 RUN.
#   - Slash-prefixed slash-command labels in macros: `'/...` survives
#     the LABEL-mode commit, and the macro pump replays each char
#     through handle_key so the bare keystrokes drive the menu live.
#     <name> binds the macro range; macros named with anything other
#     than `\letter` aren't reachable via Alt-letter and must be
#   - Alt-F3 RUN opens the NAMES overlay; ENTER on the highlighted
#   - `~` inside macro source becomes ENTER at run-time, both for
#     prompt-commit (filename, range) and for inter-step submenu
# Tutorial divergence: the tutorial's macro uses `/Print Printer`
# L123's testable equivalent is `/Print File`, which writes to disk
# and lets the transcript verify output via ASSERT_FILE_CONTAINS.
# The lesson — that `/`-prefixed sequences survive as macro labels
# and replay live through the menu — is the same.
# --- Seed two cells of data to print at A1 / B1.
# --- Author the print macro across two label cells (B5..B6) so the
# macro is well clear of the data and easy to read. The macro splits
# at a natural boundary: B5 enters the Print-File prompt and commits
# the filename; B6 specifies the range and runs Go/Quit.
# --- Bind the macro range to the multi-character name `print_data`.
# Naming only the first cell (B5..B5) is sufficient; the macro pump
# walks the column downward until a blank cell, so B6's actions
# execute as a continuation of the same macro.
# --- Park the cell pointer somewhere harmless before invoking, so
# the macro's effect is observable independent of where authoring
# --- Alt-F3 RUN opens the NAMES overlay. ENTER on the highlighted
# entry runs the corresponding macro. Names display in their stored
# --- The macro printed the data. Both cells in the range render
# their displayed text into the .prn file.
